candidate:
REWARD_MACHINE:
STATES: u0, u1, u2, u3
INITIAL_STATE: u0
FINAL_STATES: u3
TRANSITION_FUNCTION:
(u0, key_found & !has_matching_key) -> u1
(u0, has_matching_key) -> u2
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, has_matching_key) -> u2
(u1, else) -> u1
(u2, has_matching_key) -> u3
(u2, else) -> u2
(u3, else) -> u3
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, key_found & !has_matching_key, u1) -> 0.05
(u0, has_matching_key, u2) -> 0.15
(u1, has_matching_key, u2) -> 0.1
(u2, has_matching_key, u3) -> 1.0
feedback: The reward machine correctly captures the task 'Be holding the matching key on at least two different moves', i.e., has_matching_key holding at two distinct steps (not necessarily consecutive; a continuous two-step hold or a drop-and-repick both qualify). Acceptance is exact: u3 is reachable iff the agent holds the key on a second step after the first (u1->u2 at the first holding step, then u2->u3 at any later step where has_matching_key still or again holds; a single one-step hold followed by a drop leaves the machine in u2 via the else self-loop and never reaches u3). Reachability holds: see the key (u0->u1), pick it up (u1->u2), keep holding one more step (u2->u3), all feasible well within the step limits. The per-state else self-loops (u0, u1, u2, u3) cover every event irrelevant to the task, including target_door_open, target_room_entered and target_picked_up, plus key_found-only steps after the latch and has_matching_key turning false on a drop, so a later re-pickup can still complete the task. Labels are predicate-only over the given propositions with proper handling of persistent vs. non-persistent kinds: key_found is a latch and is only used for the pre-holding milestone with the !has_matching_key guard; has_matching_key as a condition correctly fires the final transition on its persistence in a later step, which is exactly the 'different move' requirement; no explicit regression transition is needed because the task does not mandate a drop between the two holdings, and the else loops already admit the drop-repick path. Ordered-transition coverage respects the constraint that has_matching_key implies key_found already held, so the milestone chain is consistent; the direct (u0, has_matching_key) transition is effectively a defensive fallback that cannot fire (the key is always seen on an earlier step before it can be picked up) and is harmless. Rewards are non-negative, dense (0.05 for locating the key, 0.1/0.15 for first holding, 1.0 on completion), and bounded: the two paths yield the same total (0.05+0.1+1.0 = 0.15+1.0 = 1.15), each reward can be earned at most once since the chain is forward-only and u3 is absorbing, so there is no reward farming or unsafe shaping. Format matches the paper style: REWARD_MACHINE header, declared STATES, INITIAL_STATE, a nonempty FINAL_STATES entry naming the declared accepting state u3, TRANSITION_FUNCTION as (source, predicate) -> target with an else catch-all per state, and REWARD_FUNCTION as (source, label, target) -> value. Minor note: state u1 is not needed for the task's acceptance condition (a 3-state counting machine would suffice) but is acceptable as a dense-progress milestone; likewise the unreachable u0->u2 edge is redundant but benign.

feedback: All five environment-declared propositions are defined with exact name alignment and no extra or missing functions. (1) key_found: correct view-based latch — previous_valuation['key_found'] OR a key (object index 5) visible in env.gen_obs()['image']; the truthiness guard on previous_valuation is harmless given it is a complete valuation (equals prev['key_found']), and degrades gracefully to the view check if absent, which is correct at step 0 since the latch starts false. Uses built-in any with plain iteration, no forbidden NumPy method calls. (2) has_matching_key: carrying is a key whose color matches a door found by place in the target room's left wall (column width − room_size, rows (room_size−1)*B … (room_size−1)*B + room_size−1, B from the ball's row with the documented agent-row fallback). Since that wall segment holds exactly one door — the locked target door — this is equivalent to carrying.color == L, and the color check survives unlocking (which clears is_locked). Short-circuiting ensures env.carrying is non-None before the scan. (3) target_door_open: is_open of a door found by place in the same wall segment — equivalent to the reference expression given the single-door layout, and correctly independent of is_locked. (4) target_room_entered: correct latch; ax >= width − room_size includes the doorway cell, rows match the room block, ball-row fallback matches the documented default. (5) target_picked_up: exact match, mission-anchored via the f-string. Persistent propositions read the previous valuation read-only; condition propositions use current state only. No imports, no actions, no mutation of env or episode_memory; empty cells guarded with 'is not None'; room size read from env.room_size so both S4R3 and S6R3 are handled; syntax is valid Python. Consistent with the recorded sandbox check that the key-in-hand-vs-target-door-color variant yields 0 errors and 0 differences across all five propositions.
